1.1 Central idea
The search will use two complementary mechanisms that were not the controlling mechanism in the previous program:

1. Exact finite-integer minimax layers. For selected even sample counts, search directly over balanced binary step functions by formulating the discrete problem exactly as a binary linear minimax model. Because binary candidate values make the products `a_i (1-a_j)` exact, this can produce a discrete proof candidate at low sample count, which is preferred by the task metric and can be much faster to optimize than fractional high-resolution steps. The binary objective upper bound for a fixed sample count is `(integer_raw_overlap) * (2 / n)`, so every valid binary assignment immediately gives a valid continuous step-function upper bound.

2. Population-based exact-objective global search over fractional and semi-fractional step functions. Starting from the parent, deterministic structured constructions, feasible rotations/reversals/reflections, and the integer candidate pool produced by the MILP layers, maintain many feasible step functions. New candidates are generated as convex combinations plus small zero-sum mutations and repaired by a joint box-plus-sum projection. Candidates are accepted and ranked strictly by the exact evaluator, not by a surrogate. Best members receive local refinement using exact line searches, gradient-like directions, and coordinate-exchange moves while preserving the sum.

This differs substantively from the previous local-smooth/log-sum/LP solver centered on one trajectory. The new method obtains diverse feasible observations before refining, then moves the global population, and prevents the method from being trapped in the supplied parent basin.
